_comment: Measured quality floors. A change that drops below any of these fails the guard.
These are FLOORS, not targets. Raise them when a change earns it, deliberately,
in the same commit that earns it. Lowering one is a decision that must be argued
in a commit message, never a convenience to make a build pass.
Two suites are tracked because they measure different query distributions and
have disagreed. heldOut queries are author prose, plentiful and unbiased but not
what production receives. agent queries are real tool stderr, representative but
few. A change that improves one and damages the other is a trade to be made
consciously, which is why both appear here.

heldOut._source: npm run cairn:eval — mechanism and appliesTo, never indexed
_note: Raised after the gap to plain BM25 was closed. The history, so the next
person can count honestly: no length normalisation lost prose P@1 0.711 to
BM25's 0.868; adding BM25's own normalisation reached 0.763; fusing BM25's
ordering at weight 0.3 reached 0.789 / MRR 0.882, and the remaining gap was
recorded here as real and unexplained.
It was one quantity the code already computed and did not rank on. The
`explained` fraction -- of the information in the QUESTION, how much did
this finding account for -- was calculated after the sort and used only to
write caveats. Five of the eight failures had the gold finding explaining
MORE of the query than the finding that beat it. Fusing it as a third
ranking at weight 1.0 gives 0.868 / MRR 0.928: level with BM25 on prose,
ahead on MRR, machine output still 1.000 and unknown ground still 3/3.
That is the first change in this file's history that was not a trade.
The five residual failures are all sibling pairs -- the top hit is a
finding about the same trap, and delivery is 1.000 because the agent is
told about the gold either way. P@1 = 1.0 on this split would require the
ranker to distinguish findings the prose itself does not distinguish.

agent._source: npm run cairn:agent-eval — real commands, real stderr
_note: silentOnUnknown counts 'returned nothing' OR 'returned only weak-labelled
matches' -- both safe; only a confident wrong answer is not.
3/3 since the failing command became evidence. Six statistical methods could
not get the third; the program name that produced the error got all three,
because it is a different KIND of evidence rather than a better weighting of
the same one.

corpus._source: npm run cairn:lint and npm run cairn:doctor

maxFalseWeak._source: fraction of CORRECT answers labelled weak
maxFalseWeak._note: If this climbs the label becomes noise and agents will ignore it.
